content: The World Health Organization (WHO) emphasizes that the designations and presentation of material in its publications do not imply any opinion regarding the legal status of countries, territories, cities, or areas, nor their boundaries. Any dotted or dashed lines on maps represent approximate borders that may not yet have full agreement. The mention of specific companies or products does not constitute endorsement or recommendation by WHO over others of a similar nature. While every effort has been made to verify the information in this publication, it is distributed without warranty of any kind, and the responsibility for its interpretation and use lies with the reader. WHO is not liable for any damages arising from its use. In 2012, Oman became the first country to be recognized as having eliminated trachoma as a public health problem. This assessment process was referred to as a verification exercise. By 2015, WHO's Strategic and Technical Advisory Group on Neglected Tropical Diseases endorsed standardized processes for confirming and acknowledging success in eliminating neglected tropical diseases (NTDs) targeted for eradication, elimination of transmission, or elimination as a public health problem. For diseases targeted for elimination as a public health problem, the process is now defined as validation. The validation process for trachoma elimination involves a two-step approach. First, after implementing interventions and at least six months following the final round of mass antibiotic administration, an impact survey is conducted. If the prevalence threshold for trachomatous inflammation-follicular (TF) is met, the district enters a two-year pre-validation surveillance period during which no further mass antibiotic administration is implemented. At the end of this period, a pre-validation surveillance survey is conducted. Standard operating procedures for these surveys are provided separately. A country meets the criteria for validation if all previously endemic districts demonstrate sub-elimination threshold prevalence levels for trachomatous trichiasis (TT) and TF in adequately conducted pre-validation surveillance surveys. Consideration may also be given to the timing of interventions and surveillance activities in adjacent districts. The Member State must prepare a dossier documenting the achievement of elimination targets, which may include assistance from WHO. The dossier should follow a template established by WHO and be submitted in both hard and electronic copies to the WHO Country Office, which will forward it to the relevant regional and headquarters offices. The dossier is assessed by an ad-hoc Dossier Review Group, which evaluates the evidence and recommends whether the claim of elimination should be validated. The group is appointed by the WHO Regional Office in consultation with the Department of Control of Neglected Tropical Diseases at WHO headquarters. The group comprises experts in the SAFE strategy (Surgery, Antibiotics, Facial cleanliness, and Environmental improvement) and validation processes, ensuring no conflicts of interest with the Member State under review. The group may also include WHO delegates who act as the secretariat. The group reviews the dossier, provides written comments, and may conduct a country visit if deemed necessary. It then reaches a consensus and recommends either validation of the elimination claim or postponement until further evidence is provided. Recommendations are justified and may include guidance for post-validation surveillance or steps for achieving validation in the future. The validation process is reversible, and countries must continue post-validation surveillance as recommended. Surveillance data should be reported to WHO, and any reappearance or recrudescence of the disease above elimination thresholds will be noted, with endemicity status updated accordingly. With the agreement of the Member State, validated dossiers may be made publicly available on the WHO website as reference documents. The dossier template is designed to help national trachoma program managers compile evidence for validation. It includes required sections on demographic and development context, trachoma program history, program overview, evaluation units, data classification, and interventions (surgery, antibiotics, facial cleanliness, and environmental improvement). It also requires information on impact and pre-validation surveillance surveys, regional context, post-validation surveillance plans, and any special issues affecting the program. Optional sections may include additional demographic details, special circumstances, and resources or partnerships. A bibliography of data sources and a list of abbreviations used in the dossier must also be included.
